title: CRLR/204/2024 of SMT ASHA BISHT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
DAILY LOK ADALAT
Criminal Revision No. 204 of 2024
Smt. Asha Bisht ........Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and another ........Respondents
Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, Advocate, for the revisionist.
Mr. Deepak Bhardwaj, learned Brief Holder for the State/respondent no.1.
Mr.Amit Kapri, Advocate for the respondent no.2 through video conferencing.
 Daily Lok Adalat Award
Present:
Hon'ble J.C.S. Rawat, J. (Retd.)
Mahesh Chandra Pant, Member/Mediator
This is a criminal revision arising out of the judgment and order
dated 12.10.2023 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Pithoragarh
in Complaint Case No. 1734 of 2020 (new no. 173 of 2022 and 176 of
2022), Mamta Bonal vs. Smt. Asha Bisht under Section 138 of
Negotiable Instruments Act, by which, the revisionist has been
convicted under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act sentencing
her to undergo for a period of four months imprisonment along with a
fine of Rs. 15,25,000/-, and the judgment and order dated 01.03.2024
passed by the learned Sessions Judge Pithoragarh in Criminal Appeal
No. 77 of 2023, Smt. Asha Bisht vs. State of Uttarakhand and another,
by which, confirming the punishment awarded by the trial court.
2. This revision was referred to the Daily Lok Adalat. During the
course of hearing this revision petition, the parties have settled their
disputes amicably and have filed a compromise before the Daily Lok

2
Adalat. It has been settled and indicating in para-5 of the petition that
the accused-appellant has paid Rs.2 lakhs and for the rest amount she
has assured to pay within a period of six months from her release. Now,
therefore, the parties have prayed that the said compromise be recorded
and the sentence and the fine imposed by the trial court as well as the
learned Sessions Judge be set aside and the accused-appellant be
released forthwith from the jail.
3. In view of the above, the matter has been settled by way of the
compromise. Both the parties have pleaded that the penalty amount
according to the guidelines laid down by the judgment of the Hono'ble
Apex Court in Damodar S. Prabhu vs. Sayed Babalal H (2010) 5 SCC
663 be waived. Learned counsel for the parties has indicated in their
affidavit that the appellant is already in jail since 16.03.2024 and she is
a lady and now they have resolved their dispute amicably. In view of
the facts enumerated hereinabove, this is a positive attitude adopted by
the applicant to come forward to resolve the matter. We are completely
in agreement with the contentions of the learned counsel for the
applicant. We are of the opinion that can be waived in terms of the
judgement of the Apex Court in Madhya Pradesh State Legal Services
Authority vs. Pradeek Jain and another, (2014) Volume 10 SCC 690.
Thus, in view of the above, the penalty is waived accordingly in terms
of the compromise.
4. In view of the above, Criminal Revision is liable to be allowed
and the sentence and fine imposed by the trial court affirming by the
learned Sessions Judge is liable to be set aside and the accused -
applicant may be released from the jail forthwith. The compromise and
affidavit filed with the application be made part of the award.

3
5. The Revision is disposed of accordingly in terms of the
compromise. The compromise-deed shall form part of this award. The
applicant be released forthwith. Let the Trial Court be informed
accordingly. Let a copy of this order be given to both the parties free of
cost.
6. All pending applications stand disposed of.
 (Mahesh Chandra Pant, Member) (J.C.S.Rawat, J (Retd.)
 03.07.2024 03.07.2024
Nahid
